summary: Hickman County, TN tower listed extant in 2014 and standing per Landforms; no build, staffing or access history found in the sources read.

events.note: Listed among extant Tennessee fire towers as of March 26, 2014

evidence.supports: Tower is in Hickman County at 963 ft elevation, listed as standing
The listing has no date of its own; the page carries a revision stamp dated 8 January 2026
Weatherly is in Hickman County on the extant list

evidence.quote: Extant Tennessee Fire Towers as of March 26, 2014

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Landforms gives 963 ft (293.5 m); OpenStreetMap tags 292 m. The gap is about 1.5 m, so the story uses the Landforms figure and calls the OpenStreetMap value close.

sources.title: Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property document)

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, staffing, fire history, access or visit information was found in the sources read. Status rests on the 2014 extant list and an undated Landforms listing. The MPS covers Division towers and lists this one, so the story describes it as one of the Division's towers only by that list; no agency fact is recorded. The MPS says two earlier wooden towers in Hickman County (Moore's Switch and Cobel) were replaced by steel towers; it does not say Weatherly was one of them or connected to them. Unfetched lead, not used: a search result (data.capecodtimes.com, a bridge inventory mirror) titled 'NATCHEZ TRACE PARK over WEATHERLY FIRE TOWER ACC' suggests the tower access road passes under the Natchez Trace Parkway, which would bear on access. The page is behind a bot check, so nothing from it is cited; a human check is worth doing. Brief coordinates and elevation match the Landforms GPX. Searches: 2 (websearch.py). Page reads: about 3 plus the MPS PDF.
